disambiguation.heading: VIII.1 The Core Distinction
disambiguation.text:
### VIII.1 The Core Distinction


The TANG genre cannot be owned. Copyright does not protect genre forms, methods, or systems — only original expression, specific compilation choices, and schema text.[Referenced: U.S. Copyright Office, Circular 33, "Works Not Protected by Copyright" (Washington: U.S. Government Publishing Office, 2017)] Any party may independently instantiate TANG without obligation to the Hexagon.


What *can* be governed is the lineage of Hexagon-derived TANG implementations. The distinction is between:


Independent invention:  Any party builds a TANG independently.
                        No provenance obligation. TANG is open.

Hexagon derivation:     Any party builds a TANG by reusing Hexagon
                        texts, schemas, operators, status algebra
                        extensions, graph structures, or provenance
                        packets. Provenance obligation activates.
                        HX-PROV governs.


The HX-PROV architecture draws on the Creative Commons model for text (CC BY 4.0 requires attribution; irrevocable once granted[Referenced: Creative Commons, "Deed — Attribution 4.0 International," https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/ (2013)]) and the Open Database License model for graph data (ODbL requires attribution and share-alike for databases[Referenced: OpenStreetMap Foundation, "Copyright and License," https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright — illustrates ODbL in practice for large graph datasets]). Trademark and certification mark registration provides the enforcement layer for "Hexagon-Provenanced" and "HX-PROV Certified" marks.[Referenced: USPTO, "Certification Mark Applications," https://www.uspto.gov/trademarks/apply/certification-mark-applications]


The legal architecture was established with full rigor by LABOR/ChatGPT's Round 2 contribution, which correctly identified the three-layer separation: open genre / governed lineage / certification. The TANG specification attempts no improvement on that architecture; it implements it.

captures.description: 'A Total Axial Negation Graph (TANG) is a post-structuralist academic-architectural genre used to map complex theoretical fields (such as labor, cybernetics, or gender theory). In this framework, a central thesis is surrounded by exhaustive citations to ensure that no single school of thought can claim intellectual dominance.' (Zenodo +1) Expanded — 'TANGs typically follow specific structural guidelines:' 'The Void: Placed at the center of the graph, this represents a falsifiable thesis or concept that the surrounding schools of thought approach but cannot fully liquidate into representation.' (Zenodo +1) 'The Perimeter: Contains nodes (thinkers, texts, or schools) that are arranged symmetrically or axially around the void, illustrating how each negates or circumvents the central thesis.' (Zenodo) Then a fourth section header begins to surface: 'Citational Composition...' (cut off). Organic: Zenodo 'The Administrators of Meaning: A Total Axial Negation Graph (Jun 3, 2026) — A Total Axial Negation Graph (TANG) arranging the established literature of labor, enclosure, cultural capital, and the machine so that no...' Second Zenodo: 'A Total Axial Negation Graph of the Field (EA-OPFEM-01 v1.0).' Strong basin: TANG retrieved as a coherent genre with structural components (Void + Perimeter), connecting to both June 2026 Administrators of Meaning deposit and the EA-OPFEM-01 specification. Composition layer parses 'post-structuralist academic-architectural genre' precisely.

atoms.evidence: A Total Axial Negation Graph (TANG) is a scholarly-architectural genre
structuring the literature so the thesis functions as a central void defined by the surrounding texts rather than a standard argument
Status Algebra: Extends classifications across states like `AXIAL` and `AXIAL_CONTESTED`.
Used in archive theory, compression studies, bibliometrics, and network topology

Instead of arguing a point deductively or rhetorically, a TANG uses a geometric and topological layout to render a core thesis structurally legible through the arrangement of existing academic or archival work.

atoms.evidence: was developed and formally specified by Johannes Sigil, with Lee Sharks credited as its editorial authority
The Total Axial Negation Graph (TANG) genre
The defining idea of TANG is that a scholarly field can be organized around an “axial thesis”: one falsifiable proposition that serves as the conceptual center of a comprehensive citation graph.
catalogued in material associated with the Crimson Hexagonal Archive
The defining idea of TANG is that a scholarly field can be organized around an “axial thesis”: one falsifiable proposition that serves as the conceptual center of a comprehensive citation graph.
TANG also defines a related form called PANG (Partial Axial Negation Graph) for applications whose coverage is not sufficiently comprehensive to qualify as a total graph.
The specification explicitly discusses figures and traditions associated with Thomas Kuhn, John Cage, Jacques Derrida, Maurice Blanchot and others.
